title: Unit Testing Typed Functions
learning_outcomes: Explain testing inputs and outputs in the context of unit testing typed functions.
Apply the lesson concept in a small TypeScript example and describe what the compiler can check.
Identify one limitation or failure case and choose an appropriate runtime check or test when needed.

content.intro: Learn unit testing typed functions through a compact mental model, syllabus-aligned subtopics, a worked example and a practical task. The goal is not to memorize syntax but to know what the type contract guarantees and what evidence is still needed.
content.why_it_matters: Professional TypeScript code needs repeatable tests, clear public contracts, and explicit failure behavior. Keep abstractions proportional to the problem and test both values and inferred type relationships.

content_blocks.title: Mental model
content_blocks.text: **Unit Testing Typed Functions.** This lesson belongs to **Testing and Quality Assurance**. Start by identifying the problem that unit testing typed functions solves. In TypeScript, separate three questions: what values your program intends to accept, what the compiler can prove from the code, and what must still be checked while the program runs. The last category matters whenever data comes from a user, file, API, storage layer, or an untyped JavaScript dependency.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics and how to use them

items.title: Testing inputs and outputs
items.text: For testing inputs and outputs, treat incoming values as untrusted until runtime checks establish the required shape. A TypeScript annotation does not validate network, file, database, storage, or user-provided data by itself.

items.title: Boundary conditions
items.text: For boundary conditions, connect the concept to a small concrete example, state the assumption it relies on, and verify the result with a compiler diagnostic or a runtime test as appropriate.

items.title: Testing failure cases
items.text: For testing failure cases, define observable acceptance criteria and test both expected behavior and a failure case. Preserve a small regression test for any bug or inference problem you fix.

content_blocks.title: Example: Unit Testing Typed Functions
content_blocks.expected_output: Runtime output: $12.00. The callable contract fixes both the input and return types.

content_blocks.title: Compile-time versus runtime
content_blocks.text: Type annotations and most type declarations are erased when TypeScript emits JavaScript. They do not validate external JSON, authorize a user, sanitize HTML, or prevent runtime failures by themselves. Validate trust-boundary inputs and test the behavior.

content.task: Create a small TypeScript example for “Unit Testing Typed Functions”. Demonstrate testing inputs and outputs, explain your assumption, and include one check that shows the expected behavior. Do not treat a type annotation as runtime validation for external input.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates at least one syllabus subtopic named in this lesson.
The type contract is explicit enough that another learner can explain what it accepts and rejects.
The learner records a failure case and distinguishes compile-time checks from runtime validation.
hints: Start with the syllabus item “Testing inputs and outputs” and define the smallest example that demonstrates it.
Ask which part is checked by TypeScript and which part depends on runtime data, the environment or a test.
For external input, start with unknown and validate the required shape before using a domain type.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a successful type check as a runtime guarantee.
common_mistakes.why: Type annotations do not generally validate data after JavaScript starts running.
common_mistakes.fix: Add runtime checks for external input and tests for meaningful failure cases.

common_mistakes.problem: Using any or an assertion to silence a useful diagnostic.
common_mistakes.why: That can hide the exact mismatch the type system would otherwise report.
common_mistakes.fix: Prefer a more precise type or unknown plus narrowing; use assertions only when a verified invariant justifies them.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a compiler setting or runtime example without checking the project environment.
common_mistakes.why: Module resolution, DOM/Node globals, JSX and tool behavior depend on the configured versions and environment.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin the toolchain, match tsconfig to the runtime/bundler, and run the actual project's typecheck and tests.

summary: Unit Testing Typed Functions is taught through the subtopics listed in the source syllabus: Testing inputs and outputs, Boundary conditions, Testing failure cases.
Prefer precise contracts and use compiler diagnostics as evidence, not as a replacement for runtime tests.
Validate untrusted data and describe environment/version assumptions explicitly.
